L110: # Current Clinical Trials
L111: We are currently seeking patients for enrollment in funded oncology clinical trials. Study goals and suitability for each patient are discussed in detail with the clients prior to enrollment.
L112: Although clinical trial enrollment may not be the best option for all patients, in many cases, clinical trial participation provides the opportunity to receive novel, cutting-edge therapies free of charge or at a reduced cost and may facilitate treatment of pets where it would not otherwise be possible due to financial constraints or lack of other therapy options. Criteria for enrollment are outlined for each tumor type below.
L113: Please direct referrals or questions to the Oncology Clinical Trials Service at 573-882-7821.
L114: Current Trials and Studies
L115: 
L116: Bruton’s Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor (BI705564) for Canine B‑Cell Lymphoma
L117: 
L118: The University of Missouri Veterinary Health Center is enrolling dogs in a clinical trial evaluating an investigational oral Bruton’s Tyrosine Kinase (BTK) inhibitor—BI705564—for the treatment of newly diagnosed B‑cell lymphoma. This exploratory, multicenter field study aims to assess both efficacy and safety of BTK inhibition in canine patients.
L119: 
L120: Eligibility includes:
L121:   * Dogs >1 year old and 10–50 kg in body weight
L122:   * Naïve, untreated B‑cell lymphoma confirmed by cytology or histology with immunophenotyping (flow cytometry)
L123:   * At least two peripheral lymph nodes ≥2 cm in longest diameter
L124:   * WHO stage II, III, or IV B‑cell lymphoma
L125:   * Adequate organ function on bloodwork and urinalysis
L126:   * Performance score of 0–1 (normal to mildly decreased activity) and life expectancy ≥1 month
L127:   * Owner consent
L128: 
L129: Key exclusions:
L130:   * T‑cell lymphoma or involvement of skin, GI tract, or nervous system
L131:   * Internal‑only disease (mediastinum, liver, spleen) without peripheral lymph node enlargement
L132:   * Prior lymphoma treatment (chemotherapy, Tanovea, Laverdia, radiation) or long‑term corticosteroids (>2 weeks)
L133:   * Hypercalcemia, MDR1 deficiency, pregnancy/lactation, or concurrent trial enrollment
L134: 
L135: Study overview:
L136: Dogs will receive oral BI705564 once daily for 3 months (84 days) at 5 mg/kg, with possible dose escalation to 10 mg/kg in certain cases depending on early target occupancy results.
L137: 
L138: The study includes scheduled evaluations such as:
L139: 
L140:   * Physical examinations and lymph node measurements
L141:   * Quality‑of‑life assessments
L142:   * Bloodwork (CBC, chemistry, lymphoma testing)
L143:   * Lymph node aspirates for target occupancy evaluation
L144:   * Thoracic radiographs and abdominal ultrasound at screening
L145: Follow‑up continues regularly throughout the 12‑week treatment period.
L146: 
L147: Potential benefits:
L148: 
L149:   * Access to a novel investigational BTK inhibitor designed to target B‑cell lymphoma
L150:   * All study‑related diagnostics, monitoring, and investigational drug costs are covered
L151:   * Opportunity to contribute to advancement of veterinary oncology and comparative cancer therapeutics
L152: 
L153: Potential risks:
L154:   * Possible drug‑related side effects (as with any investigational therapy)
L155:   * Risks associated with repeated lymph node aspirates, blood draws, and imaging procedures
L156:   * Dogs may be withdrawn if adverse events occur or if continued participation is not in the animal’s best interest
L157: 
L158: Owner commitment:
L159: 
L160: Owners must agree to:
L161:   * Bring their dog for all required study visits over 12 weeks
L162:   * Administer oral medication daily as directed
L163:   * Allow required diagnostic sampling (bloodwork, lymph node aspirates, imaging)
L164:   * Participate in quality‑of‑life assessments
L165: 
L166: Dogs may be withdrawn at any time. If a dog passes away during the study, postmortem evaluation is requested to improve understanding of treatment effects.
L167: 
L168: Contact
L169: For more information on this study please contact:
L170: 📧 cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu
L171: Please include the subject line: BI705564 BTK Inhibitor Trial
L172: 
L173: Copper-64 Utilization for Tumor Evaluation in Cats - Feline Mammary Carcinoma (ON HOLD)
L174: The University of Missouri Veterinary Medical Center is enrolling cats with mammary carcinoma into a clinical trial to evaluate the radioactive imaging agent, Cu64-chloride, in determining tumor presence and extent of disease. Cats will receive an injection of Cu54-chloride and then undergo a PET/CT scan under general anesthesia. Enrollees will need to stay in radiation isolation for 24 hours following injection.
L175: 
L176: Criteria:
L177:   * Cats weighing at least 3.8 kg
L178:   * Presence of non-ulcerated mammary mass measuring at least 1 cm
L179:   * Histologic or cytologic diagnosis of mammary carcinoma
L180:   * Naive disease or incompletely excised tumor (previous surgery such as lumpectomy or unilateral chain mastectomy acceptable)
L181:   * Good surgical candidate (decided by surgical oncologist)
L182:   * Patient able to stay in radiation isolation without constant monitoring
L183:   * No known metastatic disease
L184:   * No significant comorbidities
L185:   * No previous chemotherapy or radiation therapy
L186:   * No need for daily drug administration
L187: Benefit:
L188: 
L189:   * This study is fully funded!
L190:   * Free baseline labwork (CBC, chemistry, and urinalysis) and PET/CT scan
L191:   * Any screening diagnostics to determine eligibility is the responsibility of the owner
L192: 
L193: For more information on this study please contact: cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu with the subject pertaining to the trial of interest 【70†or fill out a short survey here.†missouri.qualtrics.com】
L194: 
L195: COTC027: Preclinical Comparison of Two Hypomethylating Nucleosides in Tumor-Bearing Dogs
L196: The University of Missouri Veterinary Medical Center is enrolling patients into a clinical trial evaluating the safety and effectiveness TdCyd and Aza-TdC, novel anticancer agents, when given to dogs with cancer.
L197: 
L198: Criteria:
L199:   * Body weight of ≥15kg
L200:   * Histologically confirmed lymphoma or solid tumor (lymphoma may be confirmed by pre-treatment biopsy or cytology)
L201:   * Solid tumors: Solid, non-sarcomatous tumor, readily accessible for biopsy, with size of ≥3cm in the longest dimension, AND a draining lymph node accessible for AND amenable to repeated aspiration (with or without image guidance)
L202:   * Lymphoma: Nodal presentation (stage 2 or greater) with at least 3 lymph nodes of ≥3cm in the longest dimension for biopsy
L203:   * No concurrent chemotherapy or radiation therapy. Dogs must be off all such therapy for 2 weeks prior to study enrollment (exception L-asparaginase).
L204:   * No corticosteroids or L-asparaginase for 7 days prior to study initiation (exclusive TdCyd and Aza-TdC administration required).
L205:   * No h ypercalcemia causing illness
L206:   * Significant co-morbid illness, which includes, but is not limited to, renal or hepatic failure, history of congestive heart failure or clinical coagulopathy
L207: Benefit:
L208: 
L209:   * Complete cost of all treatments and re-rechecks covered by study, include initial staging or adverse side effects.
L210:   * This trial is being conducted concurrently with human trials.
L211:   * Goal of identifying maximally tolerated dose as well as pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics.
L212:   * Contribute to development of an important cancer therapy.
L213: 
L214: To Participate:
L215:   * Pet owners must be willing to transport their dog to and from the treatment center in Columbia, MO for every visit abiding by specific timelines.
L216:   * A full screening will be performed prior to full study enrollment.
L217:   * Participation will require a total of up to 10 visits over 2 months.
L218: 
L219: For more information on this study please contact: muoncology@missouri.edu with the subject pertaining to the trial of interest 【71†or fill out a short survey here.†missouri.qualtrics.com】
L220: COTC033: Repurposing Vaccine Immunity to Treat Cancers
L221: 
L222: The University of Missouri Veterinary Medical Center is enrolling patients into a clinical trial evaluating the safety and effectiveness of a new immunotherapy, the Vaccine Peptide Library (VPL), when given to dogs with cancer. Studies in dogs with cancer will complement current human trials designed to test new doses and effects of this agent.
L223: 
L224: Criteria:
L225:   * Body weight between 15 and 60 kg
L226:   * Tumor biopsy or cytology to confirm diagnosis
L227:   * Solid tumor measuring 2 to 8 cm
L228:   * No mast cell tumors, cutaneous hemangiosarcomas, thyroid carcinomas, or lymphomas
L229:   * Must not have received ANY prior experimental therapy
L230:   * No concurrent chemotherapy or radiation therapy – 2 week washout period required
L231:   * No concurrent immunomodulatory therapy (including Apoquel or Cytopoint) – 6 week washout period required
L232:   * No concurrent corticosteroids – 1 week washout period required
L233:   * No hypercalcemia causing illness
L234:   * No significant co-morbid illness, which includes, but is not limited to: pulmonary metastatic disease, renal or hepatic failure, history of congestive heart failure or clinical coagulopathy, autoimmune disorders, or uncontrolled endocrinopathies
L235: Benefit:
L236: 
L237:   * Complete cost of all treatments and rechecks covered by study, include initial staging or adverse side effects.
L238:   * This trial is being conducted concurrently with human trials.
L239:   * Contribute to development of an important cancer therapy.
L240:   * At the conclusion of the study, there will be a $1000 monetary gift provided towards additional treatment for your pet’s cancer.
L241: 
L242: To Participate:
L243:   * Pet owners must be willing to transport their dog to and from the treatment center in Columbia, MO for every visit abiding by specific timelines.
L244:   * A full screening will be performed prior to full study enrollment.
L245:   * Participation will require a total of up to 13 weekly visits.
L246: 
L247: For more information on this study please contact: cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu with the subject pertaining to the trial of interest 【72†or fill out a short survey here.†missouri.qualtrics.com】
L248: 
L249: ELIAS Osteosarcoma Trial
L250: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of a vaccine-enhanced adoptive T-cell therapy (immunotherapy) following surgical intervention for specific large to giant breed dogs with osteosarcoma.
L251: 
L252: Criteria:
L253:   * Patient must be one of the following breeds: Mastiff (all types), Saint Bernard, Greater Swiss Mountain Dog, Great Dane, Leonberger, Neapolitan Mastiff, Newfoundland, Anatolian shepherd, Tibetan Mastiff, Rottweiler, Bullmastiff, Irish Wolfhound, Scottish Deerhound, Great Pyrenees, Bernese Mountain dog, Dogue de Bordeaux, Cane Corso, and Boerboel (South African Mastiff), Golden Retrievers.
L254:   * Dogs with osteosarcoma of the radius or ulna
L255:   * Patients will NOT be eligible if they have lung metastasis, infection at the tumor site, soft tissue invasion by tumor, or pathologic fracture
L256:   * Owners must be able to adhere to the strict medical follow-up and comply with study protocols
L257: Benefits:
L258: 
L259:   * The recheck exams, bloodwork, and immunotherapy treatment will befunded by the study
L260:   * 70% of surgery will be funded by the study
L261: 
L262: To Participate:
L263: 
L264:   * Study Involvement
L265:   * Treatment related to complications of surgery or immunotherapy are the responsibility of the owner
L266:   * Pet owners must be willing to transport their dog to and from the treatment center in Columbia, MO for every visit abiding by specific timelines.
L267: For more information on this study please contact: cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu with the subject pertaining to the trial of interest or fill out this survey: 【73†https://missouri.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_d5dT74Cou88Bolo?Q_CHL=qr.†missouri.qualtrics.com】
L268: 
L269: Evaluation of Laverdia-CA1 (verdinexor) for Treatment of Naïve Canine Cutaneous Epitheliotropic Lymphoma
L270: Cutaneous epitheliotropic lymphoma is a rare neoplastic condition in dogs.  Current treatment options are limited and duration of response is often short. Laverdia-CA1 (verdinexor) is a conditionally approved oral tablet for treatment of lymphoma in dogs. Laverdia has been evaluated for the treatment of multicentric nodal lymphoma but has not yet been evaluated for the treatment of cutaneous epitheliotropic lymphoma.
L271: 
L272: Criteria:
L273:   * Histologic diagnosis of cutaneous epitheliotropic lymphoma
L274:   * No prior treatment with cytotoxic chemotherapy or radiation therapy
L275:   * No concurrent Apoquel or Cyclosporine
L276:   * No concurrent steroids
L277:     * washout period of 2 weeks is required or if a patient will remain on the steroid, the patient must have been on the steroid for > 2 weeks. If a patient is receiving a steroid at the time of enrollment and is exhibiting disease progression no tapering is needed and the patient can remain on the steroid.
L278: Benefit:
L279: 
L280:   * Laverdia will be provided to owners at no cost. Owners will be financially responsible for the cost of recheck exams, bloodwork, urinalysis and treatment of adverse events.
L281:   * We hope to evaluate the objective response rate of Laverdia as an induction chemotherapy treatment for patients with naïve cutaneous epitheliotropic lymphoma.
L282: 
L283: To Participate:
L284:   * If you have a potential candidate that is interested in participating, please contact Dr. Laura Yannai at 636-332-5041 【74†or fill out a short survey here.†missouri.qualtrics.com】
L285: 
L286: Evaluation of Timing of Carboplatin Chemotherapy post Amputation for Osteosarcoma
L287: The purpose of this study is to find out whether starting chemotherapy immediately after amputation can help dogs with bone cancer (osteosarcoma) live longer. Participants of this study will undergo amputation and follow with carboplatin chemotherapy starting the day after the surgery or right before they are discharged from the hospital.
L288: Participants will be followed until they develop spread of disease (metastasis).  Data collected will be analyzed to determine if giving chemotherapy sooner after amputation can provide a survival benefit.
L289: Criteria:
L290: 
L291:   * Dogs with bone tumors who have no received surgery
L292:   * Diagnosis of sarcoma with positive ALP staining based on cytology
L293:   * Dog must undergo amputation followed by 6 doses of carboplatin
L294:   * Must undergo complete surgical excision of tum
L295:   * Patients will NOT be eligible if they have lung metastasis or previous treatment
L296: 
L297: Benefits:
L298: 
L299:   * Chest X-rays and bloodwork (CBC, chemistry) at the time of first chemotherapy will be funded by the study
L300: 
L301: To Participate:
L302:   * Pet owners must be willing to transport their dog to and from the treatment center in Columbia, MO for every visit abiding by specific timelines.
L303:   * Any screening diagnostics to determine eligibility, surgery, and chemotherapy are the responsibility of the owner
L304: 
L305: For more information on this study please contact: cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu with the subject pertaining to the trial of interest.
L306: 
L307: Gilvetmab for the Treatment of Primary Pulmonary Carcinoma in Dogs
L308: The University of Missouri Veterinary Medical Center is enrolling patients into a clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of Gilvetmab, an anti-PD1 monoclonal antibody, as a treatment for canine pulmonary carcinoma. Similar treatments have been shown to improve survival in human lung cancer patients.
L309: 
L310: Criteria:
L311: 
L312:   * Dogs with gross disease and those with microscopic disease
L313:   * No immune-mediated disease or other severe comorbidities
L314:   * No concurrent use of steroids or other immunosuppressive drugs
L315: Study Involvement:
L316: 
L317:   * Gilvetmab is given as a slow infusion every two weeks for up to 10 doses.
L318:   * CBC, chemistry, and urinalysis are performed every 4 weeks.
L319:   * Chest x-rays are performed every 8 weeks.
L320: 
L321: Benefit:
L322: 
L323:   * The study covers the cost of Gilvetmab treatment (ranges from $540 – $1350 per treatment, depending on patient size).
L324:   * Owner is responsive for recheck exams, bloodwork, and x-rays.
L325: 
L326: To Participate:
L327:   * Pet owners must be willing to transport their dog to and from the treatment center in Columbia, MO for every visit abiding by specific timelines.
L328:   * A full screening will be performed prior to full study enrollment.
L329:   * Participation will require a total of up to 10 biweekly visits.
L330: 
L331: For more information on this study please contact: cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu with the subject pertaining to the trial of interest 【75†or fill out a short survey here.†missouri.qualtrics.com】
L332: LEAH xCAR-T: Canine B-Cell Lymphoma (ON HOLD)
L333: The University of Missouri Veterinary Medical Center is enrolling patients into a clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of lymphodepleting chemotherapy and xenogenic CAR-T cell therapy in dogs with spontaneous CD20+ lymphoma. CAR-T cells are lymphocytes (immune cells) that have had a series of genes added to them that make them professional killers of any cell carrying the target molecule.
L334: This study will seek to better understand the effects of the CAR-T cells on the tumor as well as the dog’s immune system.
L335: Criteria:
L336: 
L337:   * Canine patients weighing 10-50kg.
L338:   * Patients with naive (newly diagnosed) and relapsed (pre-treated) B-cell lymphoma.
L339:   * Must be feeling clinically WELL at home.
L340:   * Must meet bloodwork requirements and have no evidence of primary gastrointestinal or lung involvement; eligibility is at the discretion of the investigator.
L341:   * Patients CANNOT be receiving immunomodulatory drugs (Apoquel, mycophenolate, cyclosporine, azathioprine).
L342: 
L343: Benefit:
L344:   * Complete cost of all treatments and rechecks are covered by study, including initial staging; $1,000 allotted for possible adverse events.
L345:   * You pet will contribute to development of an important cancer therapy.
L346: 
L347: To Participate:
L348:   * Pet owners must be willing to transport their dog to and from the treatment center in Columbia, Missouri, for every visit abiding by specific timelines.
L349:   * A full screening will be performed prior to full study enrollment.
L350:   * Participation will require pets to come to our clinic for a minimum of four visits over 28 days and until progression or relapse.
L351: 
L352: For more information on this study please contact: cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu with the subject pertaining to the trial of interest.
L353: Parasite Study
L354: 
L355: The University of Missouri Veterinary Medical Center is enrolling dogs receiving chemotherapy to see if having intestinal parasites makes the side effects of chemotherapy worse for dogs with cancer, and to compare the different types of immune cells between dogs with and without intestinal parasites.
L356: 
L357: Criteria:
L358:   * Dogs weighing >10kg
L359:   * Cytologic or histologic diagnosis of cancer
L360:   * Willing and able to undergo chemotherapy treatment
L361:   * No clinically significant diarrhea
L362:   * No previous chemotherapy within 180 days of study entry
L363:   * No autoimmune or immune mediated disease
L364: 
L365: Study Involvement:
L366:   * We will collect stool and blood samples on the day of your dog’s chemotherapy
L367:   * You will fill out a daily log sheet for the week following chemotherapy
L368:   * One week after chemotherapy we will inform you of your dog’s fecal test results
L369: 
L370: Benefits:
L371: 
L372:   * Free fecal flotation + Giardia SNAP test
L373: 
L374: For more information on this study please contact: cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu with the subject pertaining to the trial of interest.
L375: 
L376: Thyroid Sodium Iodide Symporter
L377: The University of Missouri Veterinary Medical Center is enrolling patients into a clinical trial to assess whether using special stains for the sodium iodide symporter can allow us to identify tumors that are taking up iodine after a thyroid tumor has been removed. This would limit the need for expensive thyroid scans before surgery and increase the number of dogs that could be considered for additional treatment if their thyroid cancer is aggressive.
L378: 
L379: Criteria:
L380:   * Dogs with presumed thyroid carcinoma considered likely candidates for thyroidectomy
L381:   * Patients who have received neoadjuvant radiation (external beam or I-131) or chemotherapy, exogenous iodine supplementation are not eligible.
L382: 
L383: Benefit:
L384:   * The pre-operative thyroid scan would allow radioactive iodine therapy to be considered as an option following surgery, if there were concerns that your dog’s thyroid tumor was more aggressive than usual.
L385:   * After enrollment, the study will contribute $1,500 to cover associated clinical costs. This includes coverage of costs associated with the pre-operative thyroid scan, including sedation and hospital care (approximately ($1,055).
L386: 
L387: To Participate:
L388:   * Pet owners must be willing to move forward with surgical planning and resection of thyroid and surrounding lymph nodes.
L389:   * A full screening will be performed prior to enrollment at the owner’s expense.
L390:     * Responsible for initial assessment and consultation to determine eligibility for the trial.
L391: 
L392: For more information on this study please contact: cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu with the subject pertaining to the trial of interest.
L393: 
L394: Vinorelbine for the Treatment of Canine Insulinoma
L395: The University of Missouri Veterinary Medical Center is enrolling patients into a clinical trial to assess the safety and effects of vinorelbine in insulinoma patients.
L396: 
L397: Criteria:
L398:   * Dogs with target lesion (>20 mm) or with persistent hypoglycemia after surgery
L399:   * Histologic or cytologic confirmed pancreatic islet cell tumor or neuroendocrine tumor with high insulin-glucose ratio
L400:   * Patient is a Non-surgical candidate or owner declined surgery
L401:   * No significant comorbidities
L402:   * Adequate blood work results
L403:   * Patient cannot be on any other chemotherapy drugs concurrently (can include the case which failed Palladia and if blood work results are good, no wash-out period is required).
L404:   * Patients with an expected survival < 4 weeks
L405: Benefit:
L406: 
L407:   * The primary goal of this study is to determine if vinorelbine can be used as an effective option to treat canine patients insulinomas.
L408:   * After enrollment in the trial, the trial will cover the costs associated with the procedure, including vinorelbine, chemo administration fee, FreeStyle Libre device, placement, and interpretation fee.
L409: 
L410: To Participate:
L411:   * Pet owner must be willing to transport their dog to and from the treatment center in Columbia, MO.
L412:   * A full screening will be performed prior to enrollment.
L413:     * The owner is responsible for initial assessment, consultation, and staging to determine eligibility for the trial, as well as recheck fee, blood work, and abdominal imaging test during the trial
L414:   * This trial will require a total of up to 8 weeks of participation
